AUCTIONS.answer: After a tax lien has been held long enough, the lawful holder of the certificate of purchase may apply for a treasurer's deed; the county treasurer then holds a public auction, and the winning bidder receives a certificate of option for a treasurer's deed.
AUCTIONS.quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED FOR THE PROPERTY DESCRIBED IN THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... "CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED" MEANS A CERTIFICATE ISSUED BY A TREASURER TO THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: What is sold at a tax sale here and who holds it?

AUCTIONS.answer: The first public auction must be scheduled no less than 30 and no more than 60 calendar days after the treasurer mails the notice of public auction.
AUCTIONS.quote: THE INITIAL PUBLIC AUCTION HELD PURSUANT TO THIS ARTICLE 11.5 MUST BE SCHEDULED FOR NO LESS THAN THIRTY CALENDAR DAYS NOR MORE THAN SIXTY CALENDAR DAYS AFTER THE DATE OF MAILING THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: When are tax sales held?

AUCTIONS.answer: The treasurer holds the public auction at a courthouse or at a building housing the county clerk and recorder or the treasurer, as named in the notice; it may also be held on the internet or another electronic medium.
AUCTIONS.quote: THE TREASURER SHALL CONDUCT THE PUBLIC AUCTION AT ANY DOOR OR ENTRANCE TO, OR IN ANY ROOM IN ANY BUILDING TEMPORARILY OR PERMANENTLY USED AS, A COURTHOUSE OR AT OR WITHIN ANY BUILDING WHERE THE OFFICE OF THE COUNTY CLERK AND RECORDER OR THE OFFICE OF THE TREASURER IS LOCATED, WHICH PLACE MUST BE SPECIFICALLY DESIGNATED IN THE NOTICE OF PUBLIC AUCTION; EXCEPT THAT A PUBLIC AUCTION MAY ALSO BE CONDUCTED BY MEANS OF THE INTERNET OR OTHER ELECTRONIC MEDIUM.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: Where do I bid - online or in person?

AUCTIONS.answer: The statutory notice of public auction tells interested bidders that they must register and gives the treasurer's website or office phone number for more information.
AUCTIONS.quote: INTERESTED BIDDERS MUST REGISTER. MORE INFORMATION AT (WEBSITE OR TREASURER'S OFFICE PHONE NUMBER).
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: How do I register to bid?

AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 lets the treasurer require a deposit from the lawful holder applying for a deed (39-11.5-102(5)); no statewide bidder deposit was found. Check the county treasurer's bidding rules.
AUCTIONS.question: Is a deposit required and how much?

AUCTIONS.answer: The lawful holder must bid no less than the total debt as determined by the treasurer; the bid form sets out all money due to the lawful holder, including the treasurer's fees and costs.
AUCTIONS.quote: MUST SET FORTH ALL MONEY DUE AND OWING TO THE LAWFUL HOLDER, INCLUDING ALL TREASURER FEES AND COSTS ... A LAWFUL HOLDER MUST BID NO LESS THAN THE AMOUNT OF THE TOTAL DEBT, AS DETERMINED BY THE TREASURER, FOR THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE BEING SOLD.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: What makes up the opening or minimum bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: Payment of the amount bid must reach the treasurer by the date and time of the auction, or at another time on the auction day that the treasurer sets in writing, in the form the treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder does not pay in full, the next highest bidder who pays in time is the successful bidder.
AUCTIONS.quote: THE PAYMENT OF ANY AMOUNT BID AT AN AUCTION MUST BE RECEIVED BY A TREASURER NO LATER THAN THE DATE AND TIME OF THE AUCTION, OR AT AN ALTERNATIVE TIME AFTER THE AUCTION AND ON THE DAY OF THE AUCTION, AS SPECIFIED IN WRITING BY THE TREASURER. A BID PAYMENT MUST BE MADE IN THE FORM SPECIFIED BY THE TREASURER.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: When and how must the winning bidder pay?

AUCTIONS.answer: If the property is sold to a third-party bidder, or to the lawful holder bidding competitively, the treasurer may collect up to $300 from the successful bidder for processing the public auction.
AUCTIONS.quote: IF A PROPERTY IS SOLD TO A THIRD-PARTY BIDDER OR A LAWFUL HOLDER AS A COMPETITIVE BIDDER, A TREASURER MAY COLLECT UP TO THREE HUNDRED DOLLARS FROM THE SUCCESSFUL BIDDER FOR PERFORMING ACTIONS RELATED TO PROCESSING THE PUBLIC AUCTION
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: What costs are added on top of the winning bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: The property owner may redeem before the auction by filing an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction. After the auction, a lawful holder who did not win may repurchase the certificate of option by noon on the eighth business day after the auction.
AUCTIONS.quote: A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM ... NO LATER THAN NOON ON THE EIGHTH BUSINESS DAY FOLLOWING THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER MAY REPURCHASE THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: Can the former owner redeem after the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: When the repurchase period ends, title vests in the holder of the certificate of option, and the treasurer executes and records a treasurer's deed confirming the transfer.
AUCTIONS.quote: UPON THE EXPIRATION OF THE REPURCHASE PERIOD ... TITLE TO THE PROPERTY VESTS IN THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... THE TREASURER SHALL EXECUTE AND RECORD A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO SECTION 39-11.5-502 TO THE HOLDER OF THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... CONFIRMING THE TRANSFER OF TITLE TO THE PROPERTY.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: What kind of deed or title does the buyer receive?

AUCTIONS.answer: Subject to junior lienors' overbid claims, title is free and clear of liens and encumbrances junior to the certificate of purchase. The treasurer's deed does not affect existing roads, rights-of-way, conservation easements, other easements or equitable servitudes.
AUCTIONS.quote: THE TITLE IS FREE AND CLEAR OF ALL LIENS AND ENCUMBRANCES JUNIOR TO THE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ... EXECUTION OF A TREASURER'S DEED PURSUANT TO THIS SECTION DOES NOT AFFECT THE EXISTENCE OF ANY PUBLIC OR PRIVATE ROADS, RIGHTS-OF-WAY, CONSERVATION EASEMENTS, OTHER EASEMENTS, OR EQUITABLE SERVITUDES
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: Which liens or interests survive the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: If no valid bids are received at the public auction, the lawful holder who does not withdraw the application becomes the purchaser.
AUCTIONS.quote: "PURCHASER" MEANS A PERSON TO WHOM THE TREASURER AWARDS THE CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED AS THE WINNING BIDDER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION WHO TIMELY SUBMITS PROPER FUNDS, OR, IF NO VALID BIDS ARE RECEIVED AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION, THE LAWFUL HOLDER WHO DOES NOT FILE A WITHDRAWAL OF THE APPLICATION
AUCTIONS.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
AUCTIONS.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
AUCTIONS.question: What happens to property that does not sell?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The treasurer prepares a certificate of purchase for the purchaser of a tax lien on real property sold for delinquent taxes; it describes the property and states the rate of interest and the total taxes, delinquent interest and fees.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The treasurer shall prepare, sign, and retain for safekeeping or deliver to the purchaser of a tax lien on any real property sold for the payment of delinquent taxes a certificate of purchase describing the property on which the taxes and fees were paid by the purchaser, as the same was described in the record of sales, and also stating the rate of interest and the total amount of all taxes, delinquent interest, and fees
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-117 (wording only); quoted words are unchanged.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: What is a tax lien or certificate here?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: Tax liens are sold to the bidders who pay the taxes, delinquent interest and fees, or who pay the largest amount above them (a premium); the excess goes to the county general fund.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: sold to the persons who pay therefor the taxes, delinquent interest, and fees then due thereon or who further pay the largest amount in excess of said taxes, delinquent interest, and fees. The excess amount shall be credited to the county general fund.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: SB 26-144 amended 39-11-115(1): 'shall' became 'MUST' in the last sentence; the rule is otherwise unchanged.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How does bidding work (interest bid-down or premium)?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: Redemption interest is nine percentage points above the Federal Reserve Bank of Kansas City discount rate, rounded to the nearest full percent; the state banking commissioner sets it each September 1, effective October 1.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The annual rate of redemption interest shall be nine percentage points above the discount rate, which discount rate shall be the rate of interest a commercial bank pays to the federal reserve bank of Kansas City using a government bond or other eligible paper as security, and shall be rounded to the nearest full percent.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Colorado Revised Statutes 2024, Title 39 (Office of Legislative Legal Services)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the 2024 C.R.S. title 39 printout (the newest posted); SB 26-144 (2026) does not amend this section.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: What interest or penalty does the holder earn?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The owner may redeem at any time before a treasurer's deed is executed. Under the treasurer's deed auction process, the owner must file an intent to redeem no later than seven calendar days before the scheduled auction.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The redemption may be made at any time before the execution of a treasurer's deed ... A PROPERTY OWNER IS ENTITLED TO REDEEM A PROPERTY IF, NO LATER THAN SEVEN CALENDAR DAYS PRIOR TO THE CURRENTLY SCHEDULED PUBLIC AUCTION DATE, THE PROPERTY OWNER FILES AN INTENT TO REDEEM THE PROPERTY WITH THE TREASURER.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: 39-12-103(3) quoted from the 2024 C.R.S. printout (https://leg.colorado.gov/sites/default/files/images/olls/crs2024-title-39.pdf), not amended by SB 26-144; 39-11.5-106 from the SB 26-144 session law.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How long does the owner have to redeem?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: After August 1 of the third calendar year after the tax lien sale, the lawful holder may apply for a treasurer's deed. The property then goes to a public auction; if the holder is not the winning bidder, the holder may repurchase the certificate of option within the repurchase period.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: AFTER AUGUST 1 OF THE THIRD CALENDAR YEAR FOLLOWING THE DATE OF A TAX LIEN SALE, A LAWFUL HOLDER MAY APPLY FOR A TREASURER'S DEED ... A LAWFUL HOLDER IS ENTITLED TO REPURCHASE A CERTIFICATE OF OPTION FOR A TREASURER'S DEED IF THE FOLLOWING REQUIREMENTS ARE MET TO THE SATISFACTION OF THE TREASURER: (a) THE LAWFUL HOLDER WAS NOT THE SUCCESSFUL PURCHASER AT THE PUBLIC AUCTION
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: SB 26-144 (approved May 19, 2026; effective June 1, 2026) repealed and reenacted C.R.S. article 39-11.5; read from the session law as enacted.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How does a holder get the property if it is not redeemed?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: A certificate of purchase lien may not remain a lien longer than seven years after issuance (the rule does not apply to certificates held by the county). A certificate issued before January 1, 2026 may remain a lien for fifteen years.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: No lien upon property created by a certificate of purchase issued by a treasurer on account of any delinquent property taxes or any special assessment MAY remain a lien for a period longer than SEVEN years after the issuance thereof ... NOTWITHSTANDING ANY OTHER PROVISION OF THIS SECTION, A LIEN ON PROPERTY CREATED BY A TAX LIEN SALE CERTIFICATE OF PURCHASE ISSUED PRIOR TO JANUARY 1, 2026, MAY REMAIN A LIEN FOR A PERIOD OF FIFTEEN YEARS AFTER THE DATE OF ISSUANCE.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Session Laws of Colorado 2026, Ch. 135 (Senate Bill 26-144)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: As amended by SB 26-144: the session law strikes 'fifteen' and adds 'SEVEN'; quoted with struck words omitted (read from the printed page).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: When does a certificate or lien expire?

It is a premium auction: the minimum starting bid is the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees, and bidders may bid above it; premiums are never returned and draw no interest.

The minimum starting bid for each tax lien certificate is equal to the amount of the delinquent taxes, interest, advertising and fees as shown on the SRI internet auction website. Douglas County tax certificates sales are "PREMIUM" auctions in which a bidder can choose to bid up the minimum amount due. Premiums are never returned and draw no interest

AUCTIONS.answer: The winning bid must be paid to the Morgan County Treasurer by noon on the sale day, in cash, cashier's check payable to the Morgan County Treasurer, bank check, or electronic transfer to an account the Treasurer specifies. If the highest bidder has not paid by noon, the next highest bidder who has paid in full by 2:00 p.m. is the successful bidder.
AUCTIONS.quote: Payment of any successful bid amount must be received by the Morgan County Treasurer no later than noon on the same day as the sale. If full payment of the bid amount from the highest bidder at the sale is not received by noon on the day of the sale, the next highest bidder who has tendered the full amount of their bid by 2:00 p.m. on the day of the auction shall be deemed the successful bidder

ALL.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, chapter 197 (Online Sunshine)
ALL.note: Chapter 197 contains no buyer due-diligence checklist; county clerks publish their own 'as is' / buyer-beware notices.
ALL.question: What does the law or the county tell buyers to check before buying?

AUCTIONS.answer: Property on which a tax deed application has been filed is sold at public auction to the highest bidder by the clerk of the circuit court of the county where the property is located.
AUCTIONS.quote: Real property advertised for sale to the highest bidder as a result of an application filed under s. 197.502 shall be sold at public auction by the clerk of the circuit court, or his or her deputy, of the county where the property is located
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: What is sold at a tax sale here and who holds it?

AUCTIONS.answer: The sale is held on the date, at the time and at the location set out in the published notice, during the clerk's regular office hours. The notice runs once a week for 4 consecutive weeks and no sale may be held until 30 days after the first publication.
AUCTIONS.quote: on the date, at the time, and at the location as set forth in the published notice, which must be during the regular hours the clerk's office is open ... the clerk shall publish a notice once each week for 4 consecutive weeks at weekly intervals ... No tax deed sale shall be held until 30 days after the first publication of the notice.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.note: Second and third quoted passages are from F.S. 197.512(1) (https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.512.html).
AUCTIONS.question: When are tax sales held?

AUCTIONS.answer: A clerk may hold electronic tax deed sales instead of public outcry, with electronic proxy bidding allowed. The clerk must provide public computer terminals for the electronic sale at a designated location.
AUCTIONS.quote: A clerk may conduct electronic tax deed sales in lieu of public outcry. The clerk must comply with the procedures provided in this chapter, except that electronic proxy bidding shall be allowed ... The clerk shall provide access to the electronic sale by computer terminals open to the public at a designated location.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: Where do I bid - online or in person?

AUCTIONS.answer: The statute lets the clerk require bidders to show their willingness and ability to post the deposit, and at an electronic sale to advance enough funds to pay the deposit. Each county's own registration steps are in its county rows.
AUCTIONS.quote: the clerk may require bidders to show their willingness and ability to post the deposit ... electronic proxy bidding shall be allowed and the clerk may require bidders to advance sufficient funds to pay the deposit required by subsection (2).
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: How do I register to bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: The high bidder must post a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale; it is applied to the price at full payment.
AUCTIONS.quote: The high bidder shall post with the clerk a nonrefundable deposit of 5 percent of the bid or $200, whichever is greater, at the time of the sale, to be applied to the sale price at the time of full payment.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: Is a deposit required and how much?

AUCTIONS.answer: On county-held certificates on nonhomestead property, the opening bid is the value of all outstanding certificates plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. On property assessed as homestead on the latest roll it also includes one-half of the latest assessed value.
AUCTIONS.quote: On county-held certificates on nonhomestead property shall be the sum of the value of all outstanding certificates against the property, plus omitted years' taxes, delinquent taxes, current taxes, if due, interest, and all costs and fees paid by the county. ... an amount equal to one-half of the latest assessed value of the homestead.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.note: Re-read 2026-10-29; same provision as the VERIFIED opening_bid rule in data/state_rules.csv. F.S. 197.502(6)(b) sets the opening bid on an individual's certificate.
AUCTIONS.question: What makes up the opening or minimum bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: Full payment of the final bid, documentary stamp tax and recording fees is due within 24 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays. If it is not made, the clerk cancels all bids, readvertises the sale and pays the sale costs from the deposit.
AUCTIONS.quote: If full payment of the final bid and of documentary stamp tax and recording fees is not made within 24 hours, excluding weekends and legal holidays, the clerk shall cancel all bids, readvertise the sale as provided in this section, and pay all costs of the sale from the deposit.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: When and how must the winning bidder pay?

AUCTIONS.answer: On top of the final bid, the buyer pays the documentary stamp tax and recording fees. At an electronic sale, the winning bidder's advance deposit is subject to the fee under s. 28.24(11).
AUCTIONS.quote: full payment of the final bid and of documentary stamp tax and recording fees ... The portion of an advance deposit from a winning bidder required by subsection (2) shall, upon acceptance of the winning bid, be subject to the fee under s. 28.24(11).
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.542 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: What costs are added on top of the winning bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: A certificate can be redeemed at any time before a tax deed is issued, unless full payment for the tax deed, including documentary stamps and recording fees, has been made to the clerk.
AUCTIONS.quote: A person may redeem a tax certificate at any time after the certificate is issued and before a tax deed is issued unless full payment for a tax deed is made to the clerk of the court, including documentary stamps and recording fees.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.472 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.question: Can the former owner redeem after the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: The buyer receives a tax deed issued in the name of the county and signed by the clerk. The deed is prima facie evidence that all proceedings were regular, and the grantee is entitled to immediate possession.
AUCTIONS.quote: All tax deeds shall be issued in the name of a county and shall be signed by the clerk of the county. ... All deeds issued pursuant to this section shall be prima facie evidence of the regularity of all proceedings from the valuation of the lands to the issuance of the deed, inclusive.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.note: Immediate possession: F.S. 197.562 ('shall be entitled to the immediate possession of the lands described in the deed').
AUCTIONS.question: What kind of deed or title does the buyer receive?

AUCTIONS.answer: Except as the chapter provides, no right, interest, restriction or covenant survives the tax deed, but a lien of record held by a municipal or county governmental unit, special district or community development district that is not satisfied from the sale proceeds survives.
AUCTIONS.quote: Except as specifically provided in this chapter, no right, interest, restriction, or other covenant shall survive the issuance of a tax deed, except that a lien of record held by a municipal or county governmental unit, special district, or community development district, when such lien is not satisfied as of the disbursement of proceeds of sale under the provisions of s. 197.582, shall survive the issuance of a tax deed.
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.552 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.note: F.S. 197.573 also keeps recorded use restrictions and covenants running with the land enforceable after a tax deed.
AUCTIONS.question: Which liens or interests survive the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: If there are no higher bids the property is struck off to the certificateholder. If there are no bidders and the certificateholder does not pay resale costs or the amounts due for the deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk puts the land on the list of lands available for taxes.
AUCTIONS.quote: On county-held or individually held certificates for which there are no bidders at the public sale and for which the certificateholder fails to timely pay costs of resale or fails to pay the amounts due for issuance of a tax deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk shall enter the land on a list entitled "lands available for taxes"
AUCTIONS.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
AUCTIONS.note: F.S. 197.542(1): 'If there are no higher bids, the property shall be struck off and sold to the certificateholder'.
AUCTIONS.question: What happens to property that does not sell?

AVAILABLE.answer: These are properties offered at a tax deed sale that drew no bidders, where the certificateholder did not pay resale costs or the amounts due for the deed within 30 days. The clerk enters them on the list of lands available for taxes and notifies the county commission.
AVAILABLE.quote: On county-held or individually held certificates for which there are no bidders at the public sale and for which the certificateholder fails to timely pay costs of resale or fails to pay the amounts due for issuance of a tax deed within 30 days after the sale, the clerk shall enter the land on a list entitled "lands available for taxes" and shall immediately notify the county commission that the property is available.

Thereafter, any person, the county, or any other governmental unit may purchase the property from the clerk, without further notice or advertising, for the opening bid

(8) Taxes may not be extended against parcels listed as lands available for taxes, but in each year the taxes that would have been due shall be treated as omitted years and added to the required minimum bid.

AVAILABLE.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: A tax certificate is a legal document representing unpaid delinquent real property taxes, non-ad valorem assessments, interest and related costs, issued against a specific parcel and becoming a first lien on it. The tax collector sells certificates on property whose taxes have not been paid.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: "Tax certificate" means a paper or electronic legal document, representing unpaid delinquent real property taxes, non-ad valorem assessments, including special assessments, interest, and related costs and charges, issued in accordance with this chapter against a specific parcel of real property and becoming a first lien thereon, superior to all other liens, except as provided by s. 197.573(2).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.102 (Online Sunshine)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Sale by the tax collector: F.S. 197.432(1).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: What is a tax lien or certificate here?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: Each certificate goes to the bidder who will pay the taxes, interest, costs and charges and demand the lowest interest rate, up to the maximum. Bids are in quarter-percent steps; unsold certificates are struck to the county at the maximum rate. The tax collector may require a deposit and may sell electronically with proxy bidding.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: Each certificate shall be awarded to the person who will pay the taxes, interest, costs, and charges and will demand the lowest rate of interest, not in excess of the maximum rate of interest allowed by this chapter. The tax collector shall accept bids in even increments and in fractional interest rate bids of one-quarter of 1 percent only.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.432 (Online Sunshine)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Same section: 'If a certificate is not purchased, the certificate shall be struck to the county at the maximum rate of interest allowed by this chapter'; (7) 'The tax collector may require payment of a reasonable deposit'.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How does bidding work (interest bid-down or premium)?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The maximum interest on a tax certificate is 18 percent per year. When interest earned at redemption is less than 5 percent of the face amount, a mandatory minimum of 5 percent applies, except on certificates bid at zero percent.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The maximum rate of interest on a tax certificate is 18 percent per year. ... a mandatory minimum interest of an absolute 5 percent shall be levied upon the face value of the tax certificate. ... except those with an interest rate bid of zero percent.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.172 (Online Sunshine)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Second and third passages are from F.S. 197.472(2) (https://www.leg.state.fl.us/statutes/index.cfm?App_mode=Display_Statute&URL=0100-0199/0197/Sections/0197.472.html).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: What interest or penalty does the holder earn?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: A certificate may be redeemed at any time after it is issued and before a tax deed is issued, unless full payment for the tax deed, including documentary stamps and recording fees, has been made to the clerk. The redeemer pays the tax collector the face amount plus all interest, costs and charges.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: A person may redeem a tax certificate at any time after the certificate is issued and before a tax deed is issued unless full payment for a tax deed is made to the clerk of the court, including documentary stamps and recording fees. The person redeeming a tax certificate shall pay the tax collector the face amount plus all interest, costs, and charges.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.472 (Online Sunshine)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Resolves the UNRESOLVED redemption row in data/state_rules.csv.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How long does the owner have to redeem?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: After 2 years have passed since April 1 of the year the certificate was issued, and before it is canceled, the holder may file the certificate and a tax deed application with the county tax collector. The property is then sold at public auction by the clerk.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The holder of a tax certificate at any time after 2 years have elapsed since April 1 of the year of issuance of the tax certificate and before the cancellation of the certificate, may file the certificate and an application for a tax deed with the tax collector of the county where the property described in the certificate is located.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.502 (Online Sunshine)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: The applicant also pays all other outstanding certificates, omitted, delinquent and current taxes and the costs of sale (F.S. 197.502(2)); the auction is under F.S. 197.542.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How does a holder get the property if it is not redeemed?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: Seven years after the certificate's issuance date (the first day of the advertised certificate sale), if no tax deed has been applied for and no other administrative or legal proceeding, including a bankruptcy, has existed of record, the certificate is null and void and canceled. This does not apply to deferred payment certificates.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: Seven years after the date of issuance of a tax certificate, which is the date of the first day of the tax certificate sale as advertised under s. 197.432, if a tax deed has not been applied for, and no other administrative or legal proceeding, including a bankruptcy, has existed of record, the tax certificate is null and void and shall be canceled.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: The 2026 Florida Statutes, section 197.482 (Online Sunshine)

AUCTIONS.answer: Before managing tax-forfeited land any other way, the county must first offer forfeited parcels at a public auction run by the county auditor and sell to the highest bidder.
AUCTIONS.quote: Prior to managing tax-forfeited lands as otherwise provided in this chapter, a county must first offer tax-forfeited parcels for sale pursuant to this section ... The county auditor must sell the property at a public auction to the highest bidder in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
AUCTIONS.note: Section added by 2024 c 127 art 70 s 4.
AUCTIONS.question: What is sold at a tax sale here and who holds it?

AUCTIONS.answer: The sale must occur within six months of the filing of the certificate of forfeiture or the date the property is vacated, whichever is later, with notice published at least 30 days before the sale starts.
AUCTIONS.quote: The sale under this section must occur within six months of either the filing of the certificate of forfeiture pursuant to section 281.23, subdivision 9 , or the date the property is vacated by the occupant, whichever is later. Notice of the sale under this subdivision must be provided by publication in newspapers, websites, and other forums that serve diverse communities in the county where the property is located at least 30 days before the commencement of the sale.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
AUCTIONS.question: When are tax sales held?

AUCTIONS.answer: The law allows the public auction to be held online; a county may also sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction with posted and website notice at least ten days before it begins.
AUCTIONS.quote: in a manner reasonably calculated to facilitate public participation, including by online auction. ... may sell tax-forfeited lands through an online auction. When an online auction is used to sell tax-forfeited lands, the county auditor shall post a physical notice of the online auction and shall publish a notice of the online auction on its website not less than ten days before the online auction begins

AUCTIONS.answer: The starting price is the estimated market value from the most recent assessment, and the property may not sell below it for 30 days. If no buyer pays it, the price drops to the minimum bid: the delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interest and costs.
AUCTIONS.quote: "minimum bid" means the sum of delinquent taxes, special assessments, penalties, interests, and costs assigned to the parcel. ... the initial price of the property, which is equal to the estimated market value, as determined by the most recent assessment. The property must not be sold for less than the initial price for 30 days after it is initially made available at auction. If no buyer is willing to pay the initial price, the price for the property must be reduced to the minimum bid.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

AUCTIONS.answer: A $25 fee is collected in addition to the sale price when the land is fully paid for.
AUCTIONS.quote: and upon full payment for the land, plus a $25 fee in addition to the sale price, the sale shall be complete and a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
AUCTIONS.question: What costs are added on top of the winning bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: The law provides for repurchase by an interested party before the public sale, by paying all delinquent taxes and assessments with penalties, interest and costs.
AUCTIONS.quote: Prior to the public sale required under this section, an interested party may repurchase the property by payment of the sum of all delinquent taxes and assessments computed under section 282.251 , together with penalties, interest, and costs, that accrued or would have accrued if the parcel of land had not forfeited.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
AUCTIONS.question: Can the former owner redeem after the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: After full payment, a conveyance is issued to the purchaser according to the land's status on forfeiture. Any conveyance of forfeited land reserves all minerals and mineral rights to the state.
AUCTIONS.quote: a conveyance of the land shall be issued to the purchaser as provided by the appropriate statutes according to the status of the land upon forfeiture. ... Any conveyance of forfeited lands shall be subject to exceptions and reservations in this state, in trust for the taxing districts of all minerals and mineral rights.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)
AUCTIONS.question: What kind of deed or title does the buyer receive?

AUCTIONS.answer: Forfeiture extinguishes all liens, claims and encumbrances except: interested parties' rights to surplus proceeds, redemption rights under federal law, easements and rights-of-way of holders who are not interested parties, and recorded real covenants.
AUCTIONS.quote: The forfeiture of the property extinguishes all liens, claims, and encumbrances other than: (1) the rights of interested parties to surplus proceeds under this section; (2) rights of redemption provided under federal law; (3) easements and rights-of-way holders who are not interested parties; and (4) benefits or burdens of any real covenants filed of record as of the date of forfeiture.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

AUCTIONS.answer: If no buyer pays the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have bought the property by a credit bid, and the parcel may be disposed of under the rest of chapter 282.
AUCTIONS.quote: If no buyer is willing to pay the minimum bid, the state is deemed to have purchased the property through a credit bid and the parcels may be disposed of as otherwise provided in this chapter.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Ch. 282 MN Statutes (Minnesota Revisor of Statutes)

AUCTIONS.answer: Real estate whose property taxes are delinquent is advertised and sold at public auction by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes. The advertisement is titled "Delinquent Tax Sale".
AUCTIONS.quote: The property duly advertised must be sold, by the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes, at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county ... The property must be advertised for sale at public auction. The advertisement must be in a newspaper of general circulation within the county or municipality, if applicable, and must be entitled "Delinquent Tax Sale".

AUCTIONS.question: What is sold at a tax sale here and who holds it?

AUCTIONS.answer: The sale is held on the advertised date. Real property must be advertised once a week for three consecutive weeks before the legal sales date.
AUCTIONS.quote: on the advertised date for legal tender payable in full ... The advertising must be published once a week before the legal sales date for three consecutive weeks for the sale of real property
AUCTIONS.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
AUCTIONS.question: When are tax sales held?

AUCTIONS.answer: The law requires a public auction at the courthouse or at another convenient place within the county, if that place is designated and advertised.
AUCTIONS.quote: at public auction at the courthouse or other convenient place within the county, if designated and advertised, on the advertised date

AUCTIONS.answer: The officer conducting the sale submits a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments and costs, including the taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.
AUCTIONS.quote: shall submit a bid on behalf of the forfeited land commission equal to the amount of all unpaid property taxes, penalties, assessments including, but not limited to, assessments owed to a special taxing district established pursuant to Section 4-9-30, Chapter 19, Title 4, or an assessment district established pursuant to Chapter 15, Title 6, and costs including taxes levied for the year in which the redemption period begins.

AUCTIONS.question: What makes up the opening or minimum bid?

AUCTIONS.answer: The successful bidder must pay the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale, in cash, cashier's check, certified check or money order. A bidder who fails to pay has the bid cancelled and is liable for up to five hundred dollars in damages.
AUCTIONS.quote: for legal tender payable in full by cash, cashier's check, certified check, or money order on the date of the sale. ... The successful bidder at the delinquent tax sale shall pay legal tender as provided in Section 12-51-50 to the person officially charged with the collection of delinquent taxes in the full amount of the bid on the day of the sale. ... The defaulting bidder is liable for no more than five hundred dollars damages upon default
AUCTIONS.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)
AUCTIONS.question: When and how must the winning bidder pay?

AUCTIONS.answer: If the property is not redeemed, the purchaser pays the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus the documentary stamps and recording fees before the tax title is delivered for recording.
AUCTIONS.quote: The successful purchaser, or assignee, is responsible for the actual cost of preparing the tax title plus documentary stamps necessary to be affixed and recording fees.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

AUCTIONS.answer: Yes. The defaulting taxpayer, a grantee from the owner, or a mortgage or judgment creditor may redeem within twelve months from the date of the sale. Interest on the bid runs from 3% (first three months) to 12% (last three months), and may not exceed the forfeited land commission's bid.
AUCTIONS.quote: The defaulting taxpayer, any grantee from the owner, or any mortgage or judgment creditor may within twelve months from the date of the delinquent tax sale redeem each item of real estate ... First three months three percent of the bid amount ... Last three months twelve percent of the bid amount However, in every redemption, the amount of interest due must not exceed the amount of the bid on the property submitted on behalf of the forfeited land commission pursuant to Section 12-51-55.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Code of Laws - Title 12 - Chapter 51 - TAXATION (South Carolina Code of Laws)

AUCTIONS.answer: If the property is not redeemed, the collector makes a tax title to the purchaser. The tax deed is prima facie evidence of good title, and after a further twelve months it is incontestable on procedural or other grounds.
AUCTIONS.quote: shall make a tax title to the purchaser or the purchaser's assignee. ... the tax deed issued is incontestable on procedural or other grounds. ... the deed of conveyance, whether executed to a private person, a corporation, or a forfeited land commission, is prima facie evidence of a good title in the holder

AUCTIONS.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
AUCTIONS.question: Can the former owner redeem after the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: The buyer first receives a certificate of purchase. The treasurer issues a tax deed for unredeemed property 4 to 6 years after the sale on proper application; the tax deed is prima facie evidence of title, subject to special assessments for local or public improvements.
AUCTIONS.quote: The county treasurer shall accept applications and issue tax deeds for unredeemed real property subject to a certificate of purchase not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale ... the deed is prima facie evidence of title to the property described subject to special assessments for local or public improvements.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
AUCTIONS.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
AUCTIONS.question: What kind of deed or title does the buyer receive?

AUCTIONS.answer: The certificate holder takes subject to special assessments for local or public improvements. The certificate or tax deed holder's lien is superior to all other liens except those created by junior tax sales or payment of subsequent taxes by another person.
AUCTIONS.quote: The holder of the certificate of purchase takes subject to any special assessments for local or public improvements. ... The lien is superior to all other liens except those created by junior tax sales or payment of subsequent taxes by another person.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
AUCTIONS.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
AUCTIONS.question: Which liens or interests survive the sale?

AUCTIONS.answer: Property that cannot be sold for the taxes, interest, penalties and costs is bid in for the county. The county commissioners may sell and assign those certificates at public or private sale at any time; after four years the treasurer issues a tax deed to the county for unredeemed certificates it holds.
AUCTIONS.quote: Any real property which cannot be sold for the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs shall be bid in for the county by the county treasurer. ... The county commissioners of any county may sell and assign any certificate of purchase for real property bid in for the county ... at public or private sale at any time.
AUCTIONS.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
AUCTIONS.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
AUCTIONS.question: What happens to property that does not sell?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The tax sale buyer receives a certificate of purchase describing the property, the taxes and costs paid and any special assessments. Certificates may be assigned by endorsement.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The certificate of purchase shall describe the real property purchased, taxes and costs paid and shall state the amount of any special assessments for local or public improvements. Certificates of purchase may be assigned by endorsement
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: What is a tax lien or certificate here?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The statute names as purchaser any person who offers to pay the taxes, interest, penalties and costs due; it does not describe premium or interest bid-down bidding.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: Any person who offers to pay the amount of taxes, interest, penalties and costs including charges provided by paragraph (ix) of this subsection due on any real property is considered the purchaser thereof.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14). How a county chooses among several such persons is not stated in the statute; check the county treasurer.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How does bidding work (interest bid-down or premium)?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: On redemption the holder receives the sale amount plus 3%, plus interest at 15% per year since the sale for property sold at the 1982 tax sale and later; subsequent taxes the holder paid also earn 15% per year.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: The amount for which the property was sold at the tax sale ... plus: (I) Three percent (3%); plus (II) Interest at eight percent (8%) per annum since the date of sale except fifteen percent (15%) per annum on all property sold at date of 1982 tax sale and thereafter.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: What interest or penalty does the holder earn?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The legal owner may redeem after the sale until a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted; the treasurer accepts tax deed applications no less than four years after the sale.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: may be redeemed by the legal owner after the date of sale but before a valid tax deed application has been filed and accepted by the county treasurer ... accept applications and issue tax deeds for unredeemed real property subject to a certificate of purchase not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How long does the owner have to redeem?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: Between 4 and 6 years after the sale, the holder applies to the treasurer, returns the certificate, pays fees and proves the required notice: served at least three months before applying on the occupant and the person taxed (or published if they cannot be found), and sent by certified or registered mail to the record owner and mortgagees.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: upon proper application, return of the certificate of purchase, payment of fees and proof of compliance with the notice requirements of this section ... That at least three (3) months prior to the application a written or printed notice was served on each person in actual possession or occupancy of the real property and the person in whose name the property was taxed
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14).
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.question: How does a holder get the property if it is not redeemed?

LIENS_CERTIFICATES.answer: The treasurer accepts tax deed applications no more than six years after the original sale. An action to enforce the certificate holder's lien may be started no earlier than four and no later than ten years after the sale.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.quote: not less than four (4) nor more than six (6) years from the date of the original sale for taxes ... No action provided by this section may be commenced less than four (4) years nor more than ten (10) years from the date of the original tax sale.
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.source_title: Wyoming Statutes Title 39 - Taxation and Revenue (wyoleg.gov)
LIENS_CERTIFICATES.note: Read from the Wyoming Legislature's Title 39 PDF (last modified 2026-10-14). The statute does not use the word 'expire'; these are its time limits.
